newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks up at midday but rate worries cast pall.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks up at midday but rate worries cast pall.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were slightly higher at midday but traded off their morning peaks after a renewed bout of interest rate jitters hit the U.S. Treasury market.
Stocks and bonds were both solidly higher until a mid-morning report that showed U.S. consumer confidence hit its highest level in August since early 1990.
Within minutes, blue chip stocks skidded to momentary losses, as investors showed they remain spooked by the spectre of higher interest rates.
Exacerbating the market effect of the consumer confidence report was the fact that it came on the heels of last Friday's surprisingly strong durable goods data.

"The market these days is looking for a trend," said Don Ascani, president of Global Market Strategists Inc. "We view the increase in consumer confidence as part of the fundamental picture that will provide the catalyst for higher interest rates."
The Dow industrials rose five points to 5699, after peaking at about 5711 early in the session. The Nasdaq Composite also gained five points to stand at 1144.

With trading volumes still very light, market analysts said stocks should remain locked in a fairly tight trading range at least until next Friday, when a critical monthly payroll and employment report is due, the same report that triggered a sharp sell-off in early July.

A month's worth of data after employment report had indicated economic growth slowed from its sizzling second quarter pace, but recent reports have suggested otherwise, leading some to wonder anew if the Fed will raise rates, in an effort to slow growth and forestall the prospect of inflation.
Boeing Co rose 1/2 to 90-7/8 after announcing it planned to increase production of its new 777 jet.
The long bond rose 11/32, pushing its yield down to 6.97 percent. The long bond yielded 6.84 percent last Wednesday and steadily climbed to the key 7.00 percent level Monday.

"Bonds rallied on bargain-hunting after Monday's reaching the critically important seven percent level," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "But bonds are really counter-intuitive to the data we saw today." U.S. consumer confidence rose to a new six-year high of 109.4 in August from a revised 107.0 July reading. The Treasury's auction of $18.75 billion in two-year notes was seen as somewhat disappointing.

"It's not too bad for toward the end of summer. The market has fought off some profit-taking and weakness from time to time today. On balance, it's taken a good account of itself," said Marshall Acuff, a portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.

Prudential's Wachtel said notable stock movements were largely isolated to special situations. Philip Morris shares continued to rebound, up 1-5/8 to 91-7/8. Morris's board of directors is set to meet Wednesday and investors expect a dividend increase and stock split announcement.
Boeing rose 7/8 to 91-1/4. Analysts expect it to launch next week a long-awaited stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet.
